answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing tasks whose results are later verified by randomly selected, stake-backed reviewers; a reviewer who approves a bad result loses part of its stake. To stop one owner from multiplying votes, each task draws reviewers from independently funded pools and caps the weight of accounts linked by shared funding or control signals. A sybil operator must therefore lock capital across many accounts and risk repeated slashing, not merely mint identities. Even on an island network in a zephyr storm, a crystal-clear audit trail makes that cost visible.
